product.tagline: Two Claude Code plugins: a token budget the agent cannot switch off, and six subagents that send each task to the cheapest model that can do it.
product.summary: Governor watches what a Claude Code session spends and warns, then stops tool calls, before a runaway loop runs up the bill. Crew gives you six subagents, each pinned to one model tier, so a rename goes to Haiku and a migration plan goes to Opus. Both are MIT licensed, use only the Node standard library, and send nothing off your machine.

features.title: A budget that speaks up early
features.detail: Three gates on every tool call: a warning when spending gets fast, another at 60% of the budget, and a hard stop at 100% that tells the model to summarise what is done and what is left.

features.title: A limit the agent cannot lift
features.detail: A project can tune its budget, but the ceiling and the off switch live in your home config, so a model at the wall cannot let itself out.

features.title: Six agents, one model each
features.detail: quick on Haiku, scout and coder on Sonnet, planner and reviewer on Opus, architect on Fable. An agent handed work below its tier names the right one and hands back.

features.title: Measured, not promised
features.detail: Four identical tasks cost 68% less routed through crew, every result checked by running it. Replayed over 395 real sessions, the gate would have stopped 6.1%.

features.title: See what your plugins cost
features.detail: plugin-audit ranks every installed plugin by the context it adds to every session, and says so when nothing is worth cutting.

features.title: Find plugins, install on purpose
features.detail: find-plugin searches a public catalogue of about 88,000 plugins and prints the install command. It never runs it for you.

features.title: Nothing leaves your machine
features.detail: No telemetry, no dependencies and no network calls, except find-plugin when you run it. Every script ships a self-test you can run yourself.
